newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar prices hit by talk of extra govt sale.
newsitem.headline: India sugar prices hit by talk of extra govt sale.

text.p: Indian sugar prices fell as millers and stockists took profits and talk the government may release extra sugar this month weighed on the market, traders said.
Bulk consumers and retail buyers stood back from a market retreating from its recent peak.
Fear that Indian government may release more free sale sugar for the current month halted the recent uptrend and subdued sentiment.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 15 rupees at 1,375/1,425 rupees per quintal while M-30 lost 15/20 rupees at 1,420/1,490 rupees per quintal.
Free sale sugar quota for current month is 750,000 tonnes against 700,000 tonnes released during last month.
"The government may release extra free sale quota of about 100,000 tonnes for the current month to cool down the recent buoyancy," one broker said.
Meanwhile sugar mill delivery rose five rupees to 1,325/1,335 rupees per quintal on fresh outstation buying.
